candidates.statement: Payment service returns 503 on POST /v1/authorizations (fast, ~1ms), which order propagates as 502 to gateway /v1/checkout. Inventory/redis path succeeds (200). Root fault is payment-side unavailability, not latency or DB pool.
candidates.uncertainty: Cause of payment 503 (config, dependency, crash) not established; payment metrics/logs beyond http_request absent.

report.explanation: Traces show checkout 502 caused by order receiving 503 from payment /v1/authorizations; inventory/redis succeed. Payment logs confirm repeated 503 on /v1/authorizations with sub-2ms durations, indicating immediate rejection rather than latency. Gateway metrics show 502s on /v1/checkout. Exact payment failure mechanism is unproven, so candidate is bounded to payment-side unavailability.
